title: Pooled FACS-based CRISPR Knockout Screening in Human iPSC-Derived Microglia
author: Washer, Navarro-Guerrero, et al.
materials: IV. Differential sgRNA abundances – MAGeCK – Bash.
The main arguments in the above code are:
-n: this is the output file name.

steps.title: Thaw and pellet cells
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen cell pellets on ice, then centrifuge at 1,200 g for 5 min at room temperature to collect the cell pellet.

steps.title: Lyse cells with Puregene solution
steps.instruction: Remove as much supernatant as possible with a P1000 without disturbing the pellet. Add Puregene cell lysis solution: 6.6 mL per pellet for high‑cell samples (>5 × 10⁶ cells) or 300 µL per pellet for low‑cell samples (<5 × 10⁶ cells). Vortex to break up the pellet.

steps.title: Add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add a 1:200 dilution of proteinase K: 33 µL for high‑cell samples or 1.5 µL for low‑cell samples. Vortex to mix and incubate at 55 °C overnight to improve de‑crosslinking of fixed cells.

steps.title: RNAse A treatment
steps.instruction: Cool the lysates to room temperature, briefly pulse‑centrifuge, then add a 1:200 dilution of RNAse A: 33 µL for high‑cell samples or 1.5 µL for low‑cell samples. Incubate at 37 °C for 15 min to 1 h, then cool on ice for 1 min.

steps.title: Protein precipitation
steps.instruction: Add protein precipitation solution: 2.2 mL for high‑cell samples or 100 µL for low‑cell samples. Vortex immediately for 20 s (samples should turn cloudy) and centrifuge at 16,000 g for 3 min at 4 °C to pellet protein. If the pellet is loose, re‑centrifuge.

steps.title: DNA precipitation with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Prepare isopropanol tubes: 6.6 mL isopropanol in a 15 mL conical tube for high‑cell samples; 300 µL isopropanol containing 1 µL Glycoblue in a 1.5 mL tube for low‑cell samples (do not use Lo‑Bind tubes). Transfer the supernatant from the protein precipitation step into the corresponding isopropanol tube (≈6.6 mL for high‑cell, ≈300 µL for low‑cell). Mix by inverting 50 times, incubate at –20 °C for 15 min, then centrifuge at 20,000 g for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Remove supernatant into a tube labeled WA (keep at 4 °C). Add 70 % ethanol to the DNA pellet: 1 mL for high‑cell samples, 300 µL for low‑cell samples. Centrifuge at 16,000 g for 15 min at 4 °C. Transfer supernatant into a tube labeled WB (keep at 4 °C). Centrifuge at 7,000 g for 1 min at room temperature to pellet residual ethanol, then remove remaining ethanol with a P200 (high‑cell) or P20 (low‑cell). Air‑dry the pellet for 5 min at room temperature (or 37 °C in a heat block) until it turns from white to colorless (do not over‑dry).

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried DNA pellet in DNA hydration solution: 500 µL for high‑cell samples, 50 µL for low‑cell samples (nuclease‑free water may be used if a second precipitation is expected). Incubate at 65 °C for 1 h while shaking at 225 rpm, then store overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Quantify DNA using the Qubit High Sensitivity dsDNA kit. Discard tubes WA and WB after quantification. If DNA quantity is low, adjust to 0.3 M sodium acetate and repeat precipitation. Store purified DNA long‑term at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare PCR1 primers
steps.instruction: Reconstitute all PCR1 primers to 100 µM in nuclease‑free water, then create a 10 µM working stock by mixing 10 µL of the 100 µM stock with 90 µL nuclease‑free water. Store the working stock at –20 °C.

steps.title: Set up PCR1 reactions
steps.instruction: Prepare enough 50 µL PCR1 reactions to achieve ≥200× coverage per gRNA (see Table S1). In a 15 mL or 50 mL conical tube, assemble the master mix per reaction: 25 µL NEBNext Ultra 5 Q5, 2.5 µL PCR1 Forward Primer (10 µM), 2.5 µL PCR1 Reverse Primer (10 µM), variable amount of DNA template, and nuclease‑free water to 50 µL. Include a water‑only negative control. Aliquot master mix into a 96‑well PCR plate, seal, flick to mix, pulse‑centrifuge, and run the PCR1 program (Table 8): 98 °C 30 s; 98 °C 10 s; 64 °C 30 s; 72 °C 30 s for 20–30 cycles (minimum 20 cycles; more cycles for sorted populations). After PCR, store plates at 4 °C overnight or –20 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Check PCR1 product
steps.instruction: Run 2 µL of each PCR1 reaction on a 2 % agarose TAE gel for 30 min at 110 V alongside a 100 bp ladder. Expect a single band at ~851 bp for the all‑in‑one CRISPR sgRNA v3 backbone or ~305 bp for the all‑in‑one CRISPR dgRNA v3 backbone. If the band is faint, repeat PCR for an additional 2 cycles and re‑run.

steps.title: Pool PCR1 products
steps.instruction: If the correct band is present, pool all PCR1 reactions from the same sample into a 15 mL conical tube, vortex, aliquot into single‑use tubes, and store at –20 °C (or proceed directly to indexing PCR).

steps.title: Prepare indexing primers
steps.instruction: To improve library complexity, pool the 10 µM F01–F09 indexing primers at equimolar ratios in nuclease‑free water and vortex. Each sample requires a unique single index; the protocol provides 18 reverse primers sufficient for 3 repeats, 4 sorted populations, plus T0 and unsorted controls (see Table 9). Confirm compatibility with your sequencing platform (single‑indexing).

steps.title: Set up PCR2 (indexing) reactions
steps.instruction: In Lo‑Bind 1.5 mL tubes, prepare the PCR2 master mix per reaction (Table 11): 25 µL NEBNext Ultra 5 Q5, 2.5 µL pooled PCR2 Forward primer (10 µM), 2.5 µL PCR2 Reverse primer (unique index, 10 µM), 5 µL PCR1 product, 15 µL nuclease‑free water (total 45 µL master mix + 5 µL template = 50 µL). For each sample, aliquot 45 µL master mix into four wells of a 96‑well plate (three for replicates, one for a negative control). Add 5 µL pooled PCR1 product to each of the three sample wells and 5 µL water to the negative‑control well. Seal, flick to mix, pulse‑centrifuge, and run the PCR2 program (Table 11): 98 °C 30 s; 98 °C 10 s; 55 °C 30 s; 65 °C 15 s for 10 cycles; final extension 65 °C 5 min; hold at 10 °C. Store PCR2 plates at 4 °C overnight or –20 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Check PCR2 product
steps.instruction: Run 2 µL of each PCR2 reaction on a 2 % agarose TAE gel for 30 min at 110 V. Expect a single band at ~364 bp (may appear up to ~400 bp). If faint, repeat PCR2 for additional cycles.

steps.title: Pool PCR2 products
steps.instruction: If the correct band is present, pool all PCR2 reactions from the same sample into a 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tube, vortex, and store at –20 °C (or proceed directly to gel extraction).

steps.title: Prepare agarose gel for extraction
steps.instruction: Thaw pooled PCR2 samples on ice if stored at –20 °C. Prepare a 2 % TAE agarose gel with large wells (≈200 µL capacity). Tape four adjacent wells together with autoclave tape to create a single large well per sample. Add 40 µL 6× loading dye (purple, no SDS) to each sample, vortex, flick, and briefly pulse‑centrifuge. Load ~240 µL of each sample into its well. Load 5 µL of a 100 bp ladder. Run the gel at 60 V for 90 min.

steps.title: Excise DNA band
steps.instruction: Using a clean scalpel or gel cutter, excise the ~400 bp band from each lane, taking care to leave an empty well between samples to avoid cross‑contamination. Split each excised band equally into two 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tubes.

steps.title: Gel dissolution and DNA binding
steps.instruction: Weigh the gel slices to determine mass (mg). Add 300 µL QIAquick Gel Extraction (QG) buffer per 100 mg gel (e.g., 300 µL for 100 mg). Incubate at 50 °C for 10 min (vortex every 2 min) until the gel dissolves. Add 10 µL 3 M sodium acetate, mix, then add isopropanol equal to the gel mass (e.g., 100 µL isopropanol for 100 mg gel) to a 2 mL Lo‑Bind tube. Transfer the QG buffer/sodium acetate mixture into the isopropanol tube, invert to mix, and load 700 µL onto a QIAquick spin column.

steps.title: Wash and elute DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at 18,000 g for 1 min at room temperature, discard flow‑through. Add 750 µL wash buffer (contains 100 % ethanol), incubate 3 min at room temperature, centrifuge 1 min, discard flow‑through, centrifuge another 1 min to remove residual ethanol. Transfer the column to a fresh 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tube, add 30 µL EB buffer directly onto the membrane, wait 1 min, centrifuge 1 min, collect eluate, re‑apply to the column, wait 1 min, centrifuge 1 min again. Discard the column, combine eluates from the two tubes for the same band, vortex.

steps.title: Quantify and store purified library
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration and purity using a Nanodrop and the Qubit dsDNA High Sensitivity assay. Store the quantified DNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Download and backup sequencing data
steps.instruction: Obtain the .fastq files from the sequencing provider and back them up in multiple locations (local, external drive, cloud).

steps.title: Initial QC of raw reads
steps.instruction: Run MultiQC on the FASTQ files to assess overall quality (e.g., Phred scores >30) and duplicate rates.

steps.title: Install and configure MAGeCK
steps.instruction: Install MAGeCK via bioconda (https://anaconda.org/bioconda/mageck). Prepare a library metadata CSV file with columns GUIDE_ID, SEQUENCE, GENE (e.g., chr19:58864777‑58864796_A1BG_+).

steps.title: Quantify sgRNA abundances with MAGeCK count
steps.instruction:
Optionally run both forward and reverse FASTQ files (or their reverse‑complements) to maximize mapping (expect 60‑80 % mapping). Execute:
Mageck count -l library.csv -fastq sample1.fastq.gz sample2.fastq.gz … -sample-label Sample1,Sample2,… -n count_output
Replace sample names accordingly.

steps.title: Inspect MAGeCK count results
steps.instruction: After the command finishes, locate the key output files: countsummary.txt (mapping statistics), count_output.log, and count_output.count.txt (count matrix).

steps.title: QC of sgRNA count distribution
steps.instruction: In R, load the MAGeCKFlute package and generate density plots of read counts. Verify a single, normally‑distributed peak. Check mapping ratio (>60 % reads mapped) from countsummary.txt. Compute the Gini index; low values indicate minimal sgRNA dropout.

steps.title: Differential analysis with MAGeCK test
steps.instruction:
Run MAGeCK test to compare test vs. control populations (e.g., UN vs. T0 or sorted bins):
mageck test -k count_output.count.txt -t colname_test1,colname_test2,… -c colname_control1,colname_control2,… -n test_output -norm-method control -control-sgrna <list_of_control_sgRNAs> -normcounts-to-file
Adjust parameters as needed (e.g., use library‑size normalization if preferred).

steps.title: Generate visualizations
steps.instruction:
Using MAGeCKFlute, create:
• Rank plots (sgRankView) to view FDR‑significant hits (red = phenotype increase, blue = decrease).
• sgRNA‑level Log2FC plots (sgRankView) for individual guides.
• Heatmaps of normalized sgRNA counts across the four sorted populations to confirm consistent directionality.
Check that intergenic control sgRNAs show a normal distribution centered at Log2FC ≈ 0.

steps.title: Select candidate hits for validation
steps.instruction: Prioritize genes based on: (a) magnitude of Log2 Fold Change at the gene level, (b) consistent direction across individual sgRNAs, (c) adjusted p‑value (FDR), and (d) presence of multiple hits within the same pathway.
